findings.title: DynamoDB table without point-in-time recovery
findings.description: Without a point_in_time_recovery block, DynamoDB continuous backups are disabled and the table cannot be restored to an arbitrary point in the preceding 35 days.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: DynamoDB table without customer-managed encryption
findings.description: AWS encrypts DynamoDB tables at rest by default with AWS-owned keys; this rule treats a missing server_side_encryption block as insufficient because AWS-owned keys offer no customer control over key rotation or revocation. Set server_side_encryption { enabled = true, kms_key_arn = ... }.
findings.evidence: server_side_encryption.enabled = absent (AWS-owned key, no customer control)
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: Redshift cluster publicly accessible
findings.description: A publicly_accessible Redshift cluster accepts connections from the internet, exposing the data warehouse to network attacks.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, move the resource into private subnets, and front it with a load balancer or API gateway if external access is required. Verify with `aws ec2 describe-security-groups`.

findings.title: Redshift cluster without audit logging
findings.description: Without a logging block, Redshift audit logs are not delivered to S3, leaving connection and query activity unrecorded for forensics and compliance.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in resource config
findings.description: A database password written as a literal in Terraform config is stored in state, plan output, and version control. The same holds for a secret-like variable or local flowing into a credential attribute. Reference a secrets manager or a generated password instead. The secret value is never included in findings.
findings.expected: reference to a secrets manager or generated password
findings.remediation:
Remove the hardcoded credential and rotate it immediately — it is compromised.
Reference a Secrets Manager secret instead:
data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "db" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.db.id
}
# then: password = jsondecode(data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db.secret_string)["password"]
If the value was committed to git, purge it from history (BFG/truffleHog) and rotate.

findings.title: DynamoDB table without deletion protection
findings.description: A DynamoDB table without deletion_protection_enabled can be deleted by anyone with table-management permissions.

findings.title: Redshift cluster outside VPC
findings.description: A Redshift cluster without cluster_subnet_group_name is not placed in a VPC subnet group, leaving the data warehouse outside VPC network controls.
findings.expected: cluster_subnet_group_name set to a VPC subnet group
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Redshift cluster without enhanced VPC routing
findings.description: Enhanced VPC routing forces all COPY/UNLOAD traffic between the Redshift cluster and data sources through the VPC, so VPC security groups, network ACLs and flow logs apply. It defaults to false; an absent attribute is therefore treated as disabled.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Redshift cluster snapshots do not copy tags
findings.description: copy_tags_to_snapshot is absent or false, so automated snapshots lose the cluster's tags, breaking tag-based access control and cost allocation on restores.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.
